instructions: Cut each chicken breast in half through its thickness, then cut each piece in half crosswise so you have 8 cutlets. Lay them between two sheets of plastic wrap and pound them with a meat mallet or the bottom of a heavy pan to an even 1/4 inch.
Sprinkle the 1/2 tsp pepper over both sides of the chicken. Skip the salt for now. The prosciutto is salty.
Lay a slice of prosciutto on each cutlet, folding it to fit, and put a sage leaf on top. Push a toothpick up through the chicken, prosciutto and sage to hold them flat.
Spread the 1/4 cup flour on a plate. Press the bare side of each cutlet into it and shake off the extra. Keep the flour off the prosciutto side.

Heat 1 1/2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium high until it shimmers. Add half the cutlets, prosciutto side down, and leave them alone for about 2 minutes, until the prosciutto is golden and crisp.

Turn them over and cook the floured side for 2 to 3 minutes. You're cooking the chicken to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest piece. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when there's no pink left. Move them to a warm plate and cover loosely with foil.
Add the remaining 1 1/2 tbsp oil and cook the second batch the same way.

Pour off all but a thin film of fat, leaving the browned bits in the pan. Set it back over medium high and add the 1/2 cup wine and a pinch of salt. Scrape up the browned bits and let it bubble for 1 to 2 minutes, until it has cooked down by half.
Turn off the heat. Cut the 4 tbsp cold butter into cubes, add them to the pan and swirl until they melt into a glossy sauce.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Pull out the toothpicks. Serve the chicken with the sauce spooned over the top.
method_notes: Every version pounds the meat thin, tops it with prosciutto and a sage leaf, flours it lightly, browns it prosciutto side first in oil or butter and makes a quick white wine pan sauce finished with butter. RecipeTin Eats writes its recipe for veal and gives chicken breast as the swap; it floured only the bare side, pins the sage with a toothpick and swirls cold butter into the reduced wine off the heat. Well Plated and Coley Cooks add chicken broth to the sauce, and Caroline's Cooking adds broth and a little lemon. This follows RecipeTin Eats for chicken cutlets for 4, cooked in two batches to 160°F.
